monthly_review.summary: This month shows increased intensity and efficiency but reduced volume compared to last month, with notable shifts in HR zone distribution toward higher intensities.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite 6 fewer runs and 25.5 km less volume, average pace improved by 25 sec/km and aerobic training effect increased — indicating higher-intensity, more efficient efforts this month.

goal_tracker.message: You need 25.5 more km across 6 additional sessions (avg ~4.3 km/session) to match last month’s volume. With 20 days remaining, that’s achievable with one extra run every 3–4 days — e.g., add a 4–5 km Zone 2 run on 2026-07-15, 2026-07-19, and 2026-07-23.

insights.title: Improved efficiency despite slower long run
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.46 to 13.64 m/sec per bpm — driven by faster mid-week efforts (e.g., 10.0 km @ 507 sec/km, avg HR 166) and lower HR during easy runs (e.g., 4.0 km @ 129 bpm). However, the longest run (14.1 km @ 562 sec/km, HR 141) pulled down overall pace — suggesting efficiency gains are currently session-specific, not yet sustained across endurance efforts.

insights.title: Shift toward higher-intensity zones
insights.body: Zone 4 effort rose from 15% to 23% and Zone 5 from 1% to 10% of total HR time — while Z1+Z2 dropped from 53% to 41%. This reflects intentional intensity (e.g., 10.0 km @ HR 166, likely Z4), but risks under-recovery if Z1/Z2 volume remains low.

insights.title: Cadence-stride trade-off observed
insights.body: Cadence declined from 151 to 149 spm, yet stride length dropped sharply during the longest run (70.36 cm vs. 75–89 cm in shorter runs) — paired with increased ground contact time (319 ms vs. ~300–305 ms). This suggests fatigue-induced form breakdown late in long efforts, limiting efficiency gains at distance.

insights.title: High TE density, low session frequency
insights.body: Average aerobic TE is up (+0.3), but only 5 runs delivered it — meaning each session carries ~20% more load than last month’s 11-run average. This elevates cumulative stress without proportional recovery opportunity, especially given no recorded Z1-only runs (<120 bpm) in recent logs.

recommendations.action: Do a 5.0 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) on 2026-07-15, focusing on cadence ≥152 spm and stride length ≥76 cm (use real-time Garmin cadence/stride alerts).
recommendations.reason: Rebuilds Z2 volume lost this month (Z1+Z2 dropped to 41% vs. 53% last month) and reinforces neuromuscular coordination before fatigue sets in — critical given cadence drop and rising ground contact time in longer efforts.

recommendations.action: Replace your next scheduled run with a 20-min walk or elliptical session at HR <110 bpm on 2026-07-18, logging it as 'Active Recovery' in Garmin.
recommendations.reason: Zero Z1 efforts appear in recent logs; adding true low-HR recovery will support parasympathetic rebound after 3 consecutive runs ≥10 km or ≥TE 3.0 (7/5, 7/12, and upcoming 7/15).

recommendations.action: During your next 8–10 km run, hold vertical oscillation ≤7.8 cm (current avg: 7.7–8.5 cm) by engaging glutes earlier in stance and shortening ground contact target to ≤305 ms — use Garmin's real-time metrics to pace feedback.
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation >8.0 cm and ground contact >310 ms correlate with 3–5% efficiency loss in your data; lowering both supports sustainability of current aerobic efficiency gains across longer efforts.

weekly_focus.description: Balance recent high-intensity gains with deliberate low-HR stimulus and form reinforcement — ensuring aerobic efficiency improvements translate to fatigue-resistant long-run execution.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 foundation run (5–6 km, HR ≤135 bpm)
Technique-focused tempo run (6 km w/ VO2 max warmup, vertical osc & ground contact targets)
